{{Quote|You can never escape me&hellip;|The Sith Warrior, to Starkiller|<ref name="USE">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition]]''</ref>}}
The '''Sith Warrior''', also known as the '''Dark Apprentice''', was the incarnation&mdash;created through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]&mdash;of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|darkness]] that resided within [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]], a young [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who was secretly [[Sith training|trained]] in the ways of the dark side by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. A [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] in all but name, Starkiller spent years honing his skills in [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|combat]] and [[Force power/Legends|Force techniques]] as Vader's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|secret apprentice]] and [[Sith assassin/Legends|personal assassin]]. Aside from being the depiction of Starkiller's "dark side," the Sith Warrior was essentially the culmination of what the Starkiller could have become; a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], encased in a [[Sith stalker armor|suit of armor]] painfully grafted to his body, who succeeded Vader as the apprentice of [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]].

When Starkiller infiltrated the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] for a [[Starkiller's Trial of the Spirit|third and final time]], his search for further information on his [[Kento Marek|dead father]] consequently led to his completion of the [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Jedi Trials]]. Trapped in an unconscious state during the final phase of the test, Starkiller was confronted by the Sith Warrior. After a long and brutal duel, Starkiller ultimately emerged victorious. But as he regained consciousness, the specter declared that Starkiller would never escape him.

The Sith Warrior later resurfaced on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] through another [[Force vision/Legends|Force vision]]. But unlike the event in the Jedi Temple, he appeared through Starkiller, who saw himself garbed in the same armor that the warrior possessed. As the Sith Warrior, Starkiller fought and defeated a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] in his vision, only to discover immediately afterward that the opponent was his own father.

Starkiller ultimately avoided the future that the Sith Warrior represented. He reclaimed his birth name, "Galen Marek," and re-embraced his [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[House of Marek|lineage]], just before he saved the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] from a premature end at the [[Death/Legends|cost]] of his own life. Marek's sacrifice not only prevented the destruction of the Alliance, but also spared him from the fate that the Sith Warrior represented&mdash;a life as Darth Sidious' [[Slavery/Legends|slave]], trapped inside an armored suit for the purpose of life support.

==History==
===Trial of the Spirit===
{{Main|Starkiller's Trial of the Spirit}}
{{Quote|The dark side is strong in you, but you can still be saved.|Kento Marek, to Starkiller|<ref name="USE" />}}
[[File:Galen_jeditemple.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Sith Warrior personified the connection between the dark side and the Sith assassin codenamed Starkiller.]]
In the year [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[Sith apprentice/Legends|secret apprentice]], codenamed [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]] embarked on a personal journey to rediscover his [[House of Marek|origins]]. The years of [[Sith training|training]] under the relentless tutelage of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] effectively suppressed the memories of his [[Battle of Kashyyyk (c. 18 BBY)|past]] and the [[Death/Legends|death]] of his [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Kento Marek|father]]. His search for answers brought him to the ruins of the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]], the former headquarters of the fallen [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], located on the [[Coruscant/Legends|capital]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. When the apprentice discovered a [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] inside the Temple's [[Tower of First Knowledge/Legends|Tower of First Knowledge]], a [[Gatekeeper/Legends|gatekeeper]] appeared in the form of his father and implored him to complete the [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Jedi Trials]].<ref name="TFUvg" />

As a result, the apprentice slipped into a state of unconsciousness as his mind was overtaken by a [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Within the depths of his own psyche, Starkiller was confronted by his [[Force-sensitive/Legends|connection]] to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]], personified in the form of an [[Sith stalker armor|armored]] [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] Warrior.<ref name="TFUvg" /> Though Starkiller was unaware of the true nature of his opponent, the Sith specter was also a vision of a future in which Starkiller succeeded Darth Vader as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] dark apprentice.<ref name="TFUvg" /><ref name="USE" />

As their [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]] escalated in ferocity, an attack from Starkiller caused the Sith Warrior's helmet to fall off. However, the revelation of his opponent's identity caused Starkiller to freeze from the shock of what he saw. Though extremely pale and scarred on the forehead, and with eyes that reflected a deep immersion in the dark side, the Sith Warrior possessed Starkiller's face.<ref name="TFUvg" />

[[File:Stalker_duel.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Starkiller confronts his dark side, personified in the form of the Sith Warrior.]]
The Sith Warrior pressed his attack and forced Starkiller on the defensive. As the fight continued, he alternated between his own form and the appearance of Starkiller dressed in the [[Jedi apparel/Legends|ceremonial robes]], posthumously awarded to [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] after [[Death/Legends|death]].<ref name="TFUvg" /><ref name="TFUDatabank2">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'', [[Wikipedia:PlayStation 3|PS3]]/[[Wikipedia:Xbox 360|Xbox 360]] [[Jedi apparel/Legends|Ceremonial Jedi Robes]] Databank entry</ref> Yet despite the warrior's combination of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|saber strikes]] and [[Force power/Legends|Force attacks]], Starkiller ultimately emerged victorious after he [[Shiak|stabbed]] the warrior<ref name="TFUvg" /> with a [[Rahm Kota's lightsaber|lightsaber]]<ref name="TFUn">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref> through the abdomen.<ref name="TFUvg" />

As a result, the Sith Warrior's body was consumed in a blinding flash of light. Starkiller found himself back inside the chamber where he found the holocron just before his [[Jedi Trials/Legends|last trial]] commenced. But when he looked down at his left hand, he saw the pale skin and clawed fingers of the Sith Warrior, whose voice echoed with the declaration that the apprentice would never escape his dark fate. At that moment, the vision ended and left Starkiller uncertain about the exact meaning of what he had just witnessed.<ref name="TFUvg" />

===Kashyyyk===
{{Main|Mission to Kashyyyk (Great Jedi Purge)}}
{{Quote|Kill me, and you destroy yourself.|The Jedi Knight, to the Sith Warrior|<ref name="TFUn" />}}
[[File:KentoMarekForceGhost-TFU.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Starkiller, in the armored form of the Sith Warrior, encountered an apparition of his dead father, Kento Marek.]]
During a mission on the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], Starkiller discovered a ruined and abandoned [[Kento Marek's hut|hut]]. Despite the feeling of a vague sense of familiarity, his repressed memories of the past prevented him from recognizing the ruin as the home of his father, Kento Marek. Upon inspecting the hut, Starkiller saw evidence of a lightsaber duel, and also discovered a [[blue]] [[Lightsaber crystal/Legends|crystal]] on the floor. But just as he collected the artifact, the apprentice fell into another Force-induced vision, in which he witnessed and relived a past battle on Kashyyyk through the eyes and actions of his own master, Darth Vader. Through the Dark Lord, the apprentice saw the defeat of the Wookiees, the murder of his father and his own abduction by Vader.<ref name="TFUn" />

The vision suddenly changed and Starkiller, much to his horror, found his appearance altered into the armored form of the Sith Warrior. Trapped within a body composed of both flesh and machine, the apprentice felt more mechanical than alive. Overall, his physical state felt eerily similar to what his master experienced as a [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]]. As Starkiller inspected his new form, he was confronted by another version of himself, one who embraced the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]] as a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]].<ref name="TFUn" />

Embodied and overtaken by the Sith Warrior, Starkiller activated a [[red]]-bladed Sith lightsaber and adopted the [[Form VII/Legends|Juyo]] stance because of its reputation as the most vicious form of lightsaber combat. Though the Jedi's eyes contained sorrow and pity in them, he activated his own lightsaber, which produced a blue blade, and took the defensive stance of [[Form III/Legends|Soresu]]. Starkiller lashed out in a barrage of offensive strikes, and though the Jedi's defensive strategy proved difficult to breech, he knew that Soresu could not indefinitely withstand the attacks of Juyo.<ref name="TFUn" />

As the duel dragged on, the dark side that the Sith Warrior embodied became increasingly stronger within Starkiller. When the Jedi seized the offensive, Starkiller relied on his Force abilities to counter his adversary's attacks. Utilizing [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]] to hurl jagged planks from the walls of the hut at the Jedi, Starkiller took advantage of his opponent's distraction and attacked with [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]]. The Jedi struggled to overcome the agonizingly painful effects of the Sith attack in order to use his lightsaber as a superconducting loop, which then redirected Starkiller's own attack back at himself. The resulting explosion of Force energy blasted both Sith and Jedi against opposite corners of the hut.<ref name="TFUn" />

The pain inflicted by his own attack, as well as the grizzly sight of his brunt flesh, fueled Starkiller's rage and connection to the dark side of the Force. Drawing on his anger, the apprentice willed himself upright and suspended above the floor. With one outstretched arm, he telekinetically lifted his Jedi counterpart in the air, just as Darth Vader had done to Kento Marek years before. The Jedi tried to reason with the apprentice, but to no avail. Starkiller's mind had been overtaken by the dark side, and he laughed gloatingly at his hapless opponent.<ref name="TFUn" />

With the Jedi at his mercy, the apprentice unhooked one of the lightsabers from his belted waist and impaled the Jedi's shoulder with it. He then used his lightsaber to finish off the Jedi. Despite this, the Jedi remained alive. Annoyed, Starkiller summoned the Jedi's own blade to his hand and stabbed him. When the Jedi's dead body collapsed on the floor, the apprentice felt the wave of the dark side wash over him. He reveled in the feeling, relished his victory, and saw himself as the living embodiment of power.<ref name="TFUn" />

Just then, however, someone else appeared in the hut and exclaimed his remorse over Starkiller's life as a [[Sith assassin/Legends|Sith assassin]]. When the apprentice turned, his lightsaber retrieved and drawn in less time than it took to think about it, he recognized the figure as his late father, the former Jedi Kento Marek. He looked at the body of the fallen Jedi Knight whom Starkiller killed, and then stared once more at the dark side version of his son with grief and loss in his eyes. Before vanishing, he apologized to Starkiller, whom he addressed as "Galen."<ref name="TFUn" />

===Legacy===
====The death of Galen Marek====
{{Main|Battle on Death Star I}}
{{Quote|He is dead.''"<br />"''Then he is now more powerful than ever.|Darth Vader and Darth Sidious, on Galen Marek|<ref name="SWTFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Starkiller_dead.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Instead of becoming the Sith Warrior from his vision, Galen Marek dies as a redeemed Jedi.]]
Starkiller never lived to become what the Sith Warrior represented as a vision through the Force; a cybernetic apprentice and Sith assassin of Emperor Palpatine. His master's [[Corellian Treaty|second betrayal]] on Corellia, coupled with Starkiller's attachment to his allies, ultimately left the apprentice disillusioned with the Sith and the Galactic Empire. Hence, he reclaimed his birth name, Galen Marek, and immediately embarked on a [[Battle on Death Star I|mission]] to rescue the leaders of the newly-formed [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="TFUn" />

His infiltration of the incomplete [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] culminated in a final duel between Marek and his former master, and resulted in the near death of Darth Vader. Though he was tempted to execute Vader at the behest of Palpatine, Marek chose to reject the dark side of the Force. In the end, he sacrificed his life so that the Rebel leaders could be extracted from the [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] by the ''[[Rogue Shadow]]'', piloted by [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]].<ref name="TFUn" /> Consequently, Marek's premature death prevented<ref name="SWTFU" /> his future as a Dark Lord of the Sith.<ref name="TFUvg" /><ref name="USE" />

====The clones of Galen Marek====
{{Main|Dark Apprentice}}
{{Quote|I feel nothing&hellip;''"<br />"''Nothing?''"<br />"''Hate&hellip; for his weaknesses. Disgust&hellip; for his failings. And pride for rising above them.|The Dark Apprentice and Darth Vader|<ref name="TFUII">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Dark_Apprentice_DT.png|thumb|left|200px|The Dark Apprentice, the only perfect clone of the original Starkiller.]]
Although Galen Marek was dead, the life he could have lived, as reflected by the Sith Warrior, was not destroyed completely. In secret, Darth Vader endeavored to recreate his fallen apprentice.<ref name="TFUII" /> Thus, he brought Marek's corpse to [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] and preserved it as a [[Clone template/Legends|clone template]].<ref name="DT">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'': "Distant Thunder" cutscenes</ref> With the advanced technology of the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]] at his disposal, the Dark Lord began a long and laborious task of [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] his former apprentice. The ultimate goal was to create a clone who possessed all of Marek's power and skills, but none of the emotions that Vader perceived as "weaknesses." However, cloning of a Force-sensitive subject's DNA was regarded as a theoretically impossible achievement, and thus the process was full of trial-and-error steps. But after [[1 BBY/Legends|several months]] had seen the production of various [[Aberrant clone|genetic failures]], including a [[Subject 1138|renegade clone]] who [[Escape from Kamino (1 BBY)|escaped]] from Kamino,<ref name="TFUII" /> a [[Dark Apprentice|single clone]] was successfully engineered without any of his precursors' flaws.<ref name="TFUIIDatabank">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'' in-game databank</ref>

Through the accelerated cloning process,<ref name="TFUII" /> the clone was bred<ref name="DT" /><ref name="TFUIIDatabank" /> to adulthood within a few standard weeks;<ref name="TFU2cb">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (graphic novel)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' graphic novel]]</ref> [[memory flash]]es of his progenitor's life filled him with the knowledge and experience of Galen Marek. The same process had been used on the clones who came before him.<ref name="TFUIINovel">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' novelization]]</ref> The first subjects were physically deformed and far too mentally unbalanced.<ref name="TFUII" /><ref name="TFUIIDatabank" /> The more stable versions suffered from an identity crisis, due to the fact that they possessed another man's memories.<ref name="TFUIINovel" /> The clone who proved to be "perfect" in Vader's eyes, however, compartmentalized Marek's memories and was successfully able to separate them from his own experiences.<ref name="TFUIIDatabank" /> As Darth Vader's new apprentice and the only success in a long line of failures, the clone effectively became<ref name="DT" /> what the Sith Warrior reflected for Marek&mdash;a Sith assassin completely immersed within the dark side of the Force.<ref name="TFUvg" />

==Powers and abilities==
Like [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]], the Sith Warrior was a proficient practitioner of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the]] [[The Force/Legends|Force]]. His range of [[Force power/Legends|techniques]] included [[Force lightning/Legends|Sith lightning]] and various forms of [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]], such as [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Push|Force push]], [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Repulse|Force repulse]] and [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Throw|Force throw]]. He was also, much like Galen Marek, extremely skilled in lightsaber combat. He was an expert Djem So practitioner, but also utilised Dun Moch when required. He displayed incredible reflexes and durability, shown in his first duel with Starkiller, where he manages to remain standing against his opponent for a long time and comes close to defeating him. As a "dark" mirror version of the [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], the Sith Warrior also utilized the unorthodox reverse-grip form of [[Form V/Legends|Shien]].<ref name="TFUvg" />

==Armor==
[[File:SithStalkerCloseUp.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Sith Stalker Armor, worn by the Sith Warrior during Starkiller's vision inside the Jedi Temple]]
The Sith Warrior's body was encased within a [[Sith stalker armor|suit of armor]], painfully grafted to his flesh and bone, that was designed to inspire fear in both Jedi and Sith alike.<ref name="TFUDatabank">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'', [[Wikipedia:PlayStation 3|PS3]]/[[Wikipedia:Xbox 360|Xbox 360]] [[Sith stalker armor|Sith Stalker Armor]] Databank entry</ref> The suit also incorporated [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] attachments as well. His fingers had been replaced with artificial claws with blades sharp enough to cut bone. His wrists and forearms were an amalgamation of flesh and machine, which continued up to his shoulders and disappeared under a high, metal collar that protected his neck. The skin that remained on his forearms was scorched and disfigured.<ref name="TFUn" />

The armor itself included a ribbed vest of flexible armor plates and a series of leather belts around the wearer's waist. Several [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]], ranging from Jedi to Sith design, adorned the belts like trophies. Beneath the armored suit, the Sith Warrior wore tight [[black]] garments.<ref name="TFUn" /> His face was fully concealed within a helmet that slightly resembled an [[Ubese raider armor|Ubese mask]], but with a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]]-style visor in the center of the face-plate.<ref name="TFUvg" />

The overall function of the suit was similar to the [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|armor]] worn by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. Like Vader's mask, the Sith Warrior's helmet included a breathing apparatus, though the mechanism appeared to be controlled by the wearer, as the breathing pattern was forced and eclectic. However, despite its role as a life-support asset, the Sith Warrior's armor excluded the limitations that Vader's armor possessed. Whereas Vader was physically hindered by his armor,<ref name="RODV">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> which also limited his own ability to utilize the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the]] [[The Force/Legends|Force]],<ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> the Sith Warrior retained the same speed and agility that [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]] wielded without the armor.<ref name="TFUvg" /> Furthermore, the armor preserved the Sith Warrior's ability to generate [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] and did not appear to limit any of his other [[Force power/Legends|techniques]] either.<ref name="TFUvg" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:SithStalker.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Starkiller is rebuilt within the Sith stalker armor, reflecting the future that the Sith Warrior represented.]]
The Sith Warrior wears the [[Sith stalker armor|same armor]]<ref name="TFUvg" /> that [[Galen Marek]] (codenamed "Starkiller") wore in the [[Canon|non-canonical]] [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] ending of ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''. In this alternate conclusion to the video game, Marek turns back to the dark side of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and kills his former [[Sith Master/Legends|master]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. However, he fails to [[Assassin/Legends|assassinate]] [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], and thus sustains severe injuries to his body. In order to preserve Marek's life, the Emperor encases him within a suit of armor.<ref name="SWTFU" /> As the Emperor's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|new apprentice]] and [[Sith assassin/Legends|personal assassin]], Marek becomes '''Lord Starkiller''', thus bringing about the "dark future"<ref name="USE" /> that the Sith Warrior represented during the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] level in ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition]]''.<ref name="TFUvg" />

During the fight between the apprentice and the Sith Warrior in the Jedi Temple level, the warrior occasionally shape-shifts into a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] version of Starkiller, dressed in the [[Jedi apparel/Legends|ceremonial robes]] that were posthumously awarded to [[Death/Legends|deceased]] Jedi.<ref name="TFUvg" /><ref name="TFUDatabank2" /> Hence, the Sith Warrior's two different forms represented the two versions of the apprentice's fate. In the Sith stalker armor, the warrior mirrors Starkiller's life as Palpatine's apprentice.<ref name="USE" /> As the Jedi wearing the ceremonial robes, he reflects the canon ending of the video game&mdash;Starkiller's death through sacrifice.<ref name="SWTFU" />

The Sith Warrior also appears in the [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|novelization]]. On [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], Starkiller experiences a [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], in which he finds his body altered into the Sith Warrior's armored appearance. As he [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duels]] with a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] version of himself, Starkiller all but completely surrenders himself to the dark side and is thrilled by the power he gains through it.<ref name="TFUn" />

The Sith stalker armor's appearance in the Jedi Temple DLC (Downloadable Content) level in the Ultimate Sith Edition, as well as its inclusion (via a Force vision) in the novel, effectively brings it into the canon. The Sith Warrior's voice and appearance were provided by [[Sam Witwer]],<ref name="TFUvg" /> the actor who portrayed Galen Marek.<ref name="SWTFU" />

[[File:SithStalkerArmor-TFUUSE.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lord Starkiller, successor to Darth Vader and the Emperor's apprentice]]
There are six lightsabers and extra [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] hooks on the apprentice's leather belts in this costume.<ref name="TFUn" /><ref name="TFUvg" /><ref name="USE" /> The first of these "trophies" is Starkiller's [[Galen Marek's lightsaber|original lightsaber]],<ref name="SWTFU" /> lost in the vacuum of outer space after his master's first betrayal.<ref name="TFUn" /> The other weapons include [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota's]] [[Rahm Kota's lightsaber|lightsaber]],<ref name="USE" /> retrieved from the defeated [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] during the [[Battle of the TIE Fighter Construction Facility|Battle of the]] [[TIE Fighter Construction Facility]] above [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]];<ref name="SWTFU" /> the end piece of a [[Lightsaber pike/Legends|lightsaber pike]],<ref name="USE" /> taken by Starkiller after his [[First mission to Raxus Prime|victory]] over [[Kazdan Paratus]] on [[Raxus Prime/Legends|Raxus Prime]];<ref name="SWTFU" /> one half of the [[Darth Maul's double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed lightsaber]] that belonged to [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]];<ref name="USE" /> and Darth Vader's [[Darth Vader's lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]],<ref name="USE" /> taken from him after his death at the hands of his former disciple.<ref name="SWTFU" /> Lord Starkiller's new weapon, a Sith lightsaber that features three spiked emitter guards, is included his belts as well.<ref name="USE" /> In the PS2/Wii version, the Sith lightsaber has four emitter guards.<ref name="SWTFU" />

This battle between Marek and this vision was ranked number four on ''Game Informer''{{'s}} "Top 10 video game shadowselves" in [[April]] [[2009]]. It came just behind the likes of [[W:c:zelda:Dark Link (Ocarina of Time)|Dark Link]] from [[W:c:zelda:The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time|''The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time'']], [[W:c:finalfantasy:Cecil Harvey|Cecil's]] duel with his Dark Knight form so he could become a paladin from [[W:c:finalfantasy:Final Fantasy IV|''Final Fantasy IV'']], and [[W:c:metroid:Dark Samus|Dark Samus]] from the [[W:c:metroid:Metroid %28series%29|''Metroid'']] series' [[W:c:metroid:Metroid Prime Trilogy|''Metroid Prime Trilogy'']] coming in at number one.
